name: Technique - Gun click and transient
description: Standalone technique from the machine-gun checklist: a short high click layer, peak EQ and disperser for the gun's front edge.

manual.instruction: Choose a very short percussion or noise source. Trim it so it ends before the bass body develops.
manual.verify: The click is a transient, not a second sustained sound.
manual.why: MOONBOY uses a percussion transient layer; Code: Pandorum adds a short noise click.

manual.instruction: EQ a peak at the click's strongest point and remove low end. The high layer should add attack without masking the sub.
manual.verify: The click cuts through on small speakers while the low end stays clean.
manual.why: MOONBOY EQ's the peak of the transient layer; Code: Pandorum removes low end from the click.

manual.instruction: Add a disperser, or stack several gentle EQ boosts, to make the transient less digital and more watery.
manual.verify: The front edge has a distinctive shape rather than a generic sample attack.
manual.why: MOONBOY demonstrates a disperser and an EQ-based alternative on the transient layer.

manual.instruction: Blend the click under the body and check the full gun in mono. If it sounds like a separate sample, shorten it and lower it.
manual.verify: The click reads as part of one gun hit.
manual.why: The layer has to support the body, not sit on top of it.

notes: Sources: MOONBOY, 'HOW TO TEAROUT DUBSTEP' (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nApsgDWSQ7Y); Code: Pandorum, 'MACHINE GUN BASS DESIGN' (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sk--QbE_TM0); Wheysted Music, 'SERUM TEAR-OUT GUN BASS TUTORIAL' (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KkXF4T_WPbY); Dripment, '2 TEAROUT Serum 2 BASS ROUTINES' (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NRfK34KZIf8).
